key_themes: Tech/AI sell-off led by Oracle dilution fears dragged Nasdaq lower
Oil plunges 7.6% on US-Iran diplomatic hopes, lifting travel and industrials
Earnings season in full swing: Apple, Palantir, IDEXX, Tempus AI, Marriott all reported

stocks.discussion_driver: IDEXX reported Q3 EPS of $4.01, beating the $3.71 estimate, with Q3 revenue of $1.21B also topping forecasts. The company raised full-year 2026 guidance, sending shares up ~22%. Despite softer U.S. clinic visit volumes, higher diagnostic testing frequency per visit drove the beat. Post-earnings analyst price targets cluster in the $627–$750 range.
bull_case: Q3 EPS beat by $0.30 with full-year 2026 guidance raised, signaling sustained operational momentum despite softer clinic traffic trends
Recurring revenue from growing installed base of diagnostic instruments across global veterinary clinics provides durable, high-margin revenue streams
bear_case: Declining U.S. clinic visit volumes could weigh on consumables revenue growth if testing-per-visit offsets fade or plateau
Forward valuation remains elevated at ~37x forward P/E, leaving little margin for any guidance shortfall or macro deterioration

stocks.discussion_driver: Apple reported fiscal Q4 2026 earnings on November 2 with iPhone 18 Pro driving an 18% YoY surge in iPhone revenue and a top-line beat. However, shares slipped ~1.8% as management guided for weaker margins in coming quarters, dimming the profitability outlook. The stock sits near its 52-week high and analyst consensus target with limited near-term upside.
bull_case: iPhone 18 Pro demand drove 18% YoY iPhone sales growth and a revenue beat, demonstrating continued consumer appetite for Apple's premium hardware cycle
Services segment continues compounding at high margins, providing durable recurring revenue that reduces dependence on hardware unit volumes
bear_case: Management guided for weaker gross margins in upcoming quarters, raising concerns about profitability trajectory and potentially capping multiple expansion
Stock trades near 40x trailing P/E and at analyst consensus price target, leaving minimal upside on current Street estimates

stocks.discussion_driver: Palantir reported Q3 2026 revenue of $2.31B, up 96% YoY, beating estimates and raising its full-year outlook on the back of accelerating AI Platform adoption. Despite the strong print, shares fell 3.1% on November 2 and dipped further in after-hours trading as investors weigh whether the extraordinary growth justifies a 157x trailing P/E multiple. The stock is 16% below its October 52-week high.
bull_case: Q3 revenue grew 96% YoY to $2.31B with raised full-year guidance, reflecting rapid AI Platform (AIP) adoption across both government and commercial clients
Expanding commercial segment diversifies revenue beyond government contracts and positions Palantir as a key enterprise AI infrastructure vendor
bear_case: Trailing P/E of ~157x and forward P/E of ~97x are extreme even for a high-growth software company, making the stock highly vulnerable to any growth deceleration
Shares have declined 16% from the October 52-week high and fell further after Q3 earnings, signaling investor caution at current valuation levels

stocks.discussion_driver: Tempus AI reported Q3 2026 revenue of $411.5M, up 23% YoY, beating estimates and raising full-year 2026 guidance to $1.60–1.605B. Shares surged ~9% on November 2, aided by a multi-year data partnership with Bristol Myers Squibb. Despite strong growth, the company remains GAAP loss-making and shares have now run past the average analyst price target of ~$75.
bull_case: Q3 revenue of $411.5M grew 23% YoY with raised full-year guidance, and pharma data deals (Bristol Myers Squibb) establish recurring high-value AI-driven revenue streams
Narrowing GAAP losses combined with accelerating top-line growth suggest a credible path toward profitability as the AI drug discovery market scales
bear_case: Company remains GAAP unprofitable with TTM EPS of -$1.44 and no trailing P/E, making traditional valuation difficult and the stock sensitive to sentiment shifts
Shares trade above the ~$75 analyst consensus target following the earnings surge, suggesting Street forecasts have not yet caught up with the stock price

stocks.discussion_driver: Marriott beat Q3 estimates with adjusted EPS of $3.02 vs. the $2.84 consensus and raised its full-year profit outlook, sending shares to a new 52-week intraday high of $433.30 on November 2. The stock also caught a sector-wide tailwind from oil prices plunging 7.6% on US-Iran diplomatic progress, meaningfully lowering the travel sector's cost outlook. However, shares now trade above the average analyst price target of ~$391.
bull_case: Q3 EPS of $3.02 beat estimates by $0.18 with raised full-year guidance, supported by resilient travel demand and strong group and leisure bookings
Oil price plunge of 7.6% driven by US-Iran diplomatic progress improves the structural cost outlook for the travel sector and should support hotel occupancy trends
bear_case: Shares have outrun analyst consensus target (~$391 vs. ~$419 current price), suggesting that the Q3 beat and oil tailwind are already priced in at current levels
A reversal in oil prices or deterioration in global macro conditions could quickly unwind the travel sector's post-earnings tailwind
